title: Flush the DNS cache on macOS
summary: When a website opens at an old or wrong address, the Mac may still be using a saved DNS lookup. Clearing the DNS cache and restarting the mDNSResponder service makes the Mac look up website addresses again.

prerequisites: An administrator account on the Mac and its password

steps.explain: Clear the saved DNS lookup cache. Terminal asks for your administrator password; the password does not show on screen while you type it.
steps.expect: No message appears when the cache is cleared. The command line returns with a new prompt.

steps.explain: Tell the DNS service mDNSResponder to reload, so it drops the answers it saved. The service keeps running; only the signal is sent.
steps.expect: No message appears when the signal is sent. The command line returns with a new prompt.

alternatives.explain: Stop the mDNSResponder service completely (default TERM signal). The system starts it again automatically.
alternatives.expect: No message appears when the service is stopped.

verify.expect: Lines starting with 'name: apple.com' and 'ip_address:' show the address the Mac gets now.

rollback.explain: Nothing to undo. The DNS cache fills again as you open websites. If a site still shows a wrong address, check the router or the site's own DNS settings.

warnings: Flushing the DNS cache only clears saved lookups. It does not change Wi-Fi, network or DNS settings.
The commands need administrator rights (sudo). Enter the password only into a Terminal window you trust.
Right after the flush, the next websites may open a little slower while the cache fills again.
If a site is still wrong after these steps, the cause may be on the site's side or in the router, not in the Mac.
